content.text:
**Resubmitted — T4C: deviation (preferred level).**

Minimality defect repaired: the recital "Corio is the customer under this Agreement, and such customer" has been deleted. § 11.2A now reads exactly as the verifier specified:

> 11.2A Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio, on a pro-rata basis, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Naming Corio directly carries the customer-side right while sidestepping the § 1.6 `"CUSTOMER(S)"` definition (Corio's sublicensees), so the earlier ambiguity is gone rather than merely tolerated.

Unchanged and validated (`ok:true`, minimality clean):
- One insertion for an absent clause; §§ 11.1–11.3 and Exhibit B retained verbatim, no dangling cross-references.
- "or any Order Form" and "in whole or in part" omitted — no Order Form or partial-termination structure here.
- Element 4 remains **already_met** on the verbatim § 11.2 quote; § 11.1's 30-day non-renewal notice stays under RENEWAL and is not double-flagged.
- 30 days is deliberately outside the 60–90 day fallback band because the preferred level is complete and 30 days is the stronger customer outcome; fallback offered in the comment.
